The I-HAB includes contributions from USA, Japan and Canada. The Cislunar Gateway is a multi-element infrastructure designed to support both robotic and human exploration of cis-lunar space and act as a basecamp for sustained lunar exploration. The Lunar Gateway is smaller than the ISS and will require less launches for its assembly. It is intended to be occupied by a crew of up to four astronauts for periods ranging from two weeks to two months, but otherwise operates as a robotic spacecraft.The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the contractor Data Handling Special Check Out Equipment (DH-SCOE) in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.The Data Handling Special Check Out Equipment (and DH-SCOE) is part of the support equipment to integrate and test the I-HAB Gateway module.
The Data Handling Special Check Out Equipment (DH-SCOE) function is to handle MIL-1553 buses, RS-422 serial lines, command & control of I-HAB module/units over TTEthernet and simulate I/O signals Notwithstanding the complete list of countries identified in the Special Provision for visibility purposes, the ITT letter of invitation will contain a dedicated set of geographical return requirements/targets to be considered.Further information concerning the I-HAB can be found on the Agencys website here:https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Human_and_Robotic_Exploration/Gateway_to_the_Moon
